title: Impact of Houthis' Attacks in Red Sea on Singapore's Maritime Security
what_it_is: Impact of Houthis' Attacks in Red Sea on Singapore's Maritime Security

sections.label: Houthi attacks on merchant ships
sections.summary: As of 7 January 2024, Yemen-based Houthi forces unlawfully attacked 15 merchant ships in the Red Sea using missiles, drones and hijack attempts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As of 7 January 2024, the Yemen-based Houthi forces have unlawfully attacked 15 merchant ships in the Red Sea through firing of missiles, drones and hijack attempts.

sections.label: Singapore joins Operation Prosperity Guardian
sections.summary: Singapore will participate in Operation Prosperity Guardian and contribute to CTF 153's efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Singapore will participate in Operation Prosperity Guardian and contribute to CTF 153's efforts.

sections.label: SAF deployments to CTF 153
sections.summary: The SAF will deploy planners, an Information Fusion Centre team, and a Senior National Representative to the Combined Maritime Forces in Bahrain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For CTF 153 and the current Operation Prosperity Guardian, the SAF will deploy a team of planners, to work with international partners at their headquarters to formulate plans; a team from the Republic Singapore Navy's (RSN's) Information Fusion Centre to support information-sharing and engagement outreach with the commercial shipping community; and a Senior National Representative to the Combined Maritime Forces in Bahrain.

sections.label: SAF medical team deployment
sections.summary: The SAF has accepted the offer and plans are underway to deploy a medical team to aid civilian casualties there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The SAF has accepted the offer and plans are underway to deploy this medical team to aid civilian casualties there.

sections.label: Red Sea contribution and diplomacy
sections.summary: Singapore's CTF 153 contribution is consistent with its principles, littoral states have primary responsibility, and it encourages diplomatic solutions and watches the humanitarian situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: As I took pains to elaborate, our contribution to CTF 153 has been consistent with the principles that we have articulated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we recognise and we have articulated that the littoral states have the primary responsibility and there must be sufficient efforts there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That is why we encourage the littoral states and other countries, to work towards a diplomatic solution so that the Red Sea problem can be mitigated.
Apart from that, we are also watching, as I said, the humanitarian situation unfolding and where we can contribute and, we think, meaningfully, we will do so.
